text: As a finance guy myself, it is hard for me to walk past videos like this. So this guy claims that according to some index, there are only 5 companies that were founded by women, run by women, and that were IPO'd in the last 10 years. And if you invested in them 5 years ago, your return would have been minus 91%. The first thing you guys need to understand is that videos like this are generally emotionally charged. They are usually not designed to search for the truth. They are designed to paint a certain group, in this case, female corporate leadership, in a bad light. Why am I saying this? Because women are already heavily underrepresented in top corporate leadership. So if you genuinely wanted to check how well public companies run by women perform, you could simply look at companies with female CEOs and compare them with similar companies led by male CEOs, preferably from the same industries, of similar sizes, and over the same period. Because the creator knew that the result would be very different from the message he wanted to push. So run by women was not enough. He also had to choose an example that added founded by women and IPO'd by women within the last 10 years. And you know what is funny? Even with all those extremely specific conditions, there were not only 5 companies. I didn't conduct a complete academic investigation, but even a relatively quick search gives you around 15 companies that appear to meet those criteria. Yes, somewhere a woman was a co-founder, and somewhere I think a woman relaunched a bankrupt But still, in my opinion, it generally fits the criteria. So yeah, even within his very biased example, he was simply wrong. And to be fair, it is true that most of the mentioned companies performed pretty badly. Out of those 15 companies, 3 made money, while 12 lost money. But first of all, this is an extremely small sample. And second, most IPOs perform badly, including companies founded and run by men. Historical research on thousands of US IPOs found that up to 5 years, 39.7% had buy and hold return of more than minus 50%, and additionally 17.4% had buy and hold return between 0 and minus 50%. And the 2020 and 2021 IPO cohorts, which were overwhelmingly made up of male-founded and male-led companies, performed particularly badly. The creator also doesn't explain how he or whoever did it constructed the so-called index. He doesn't provide the complete list of companies examined, why other qualifying companies were excluded, what exactly starting date was used, how the companies were weighted, or exactly how 91% loss was calculated. So this is not a proper comparison between men and women. It is a hand-picked basket of 5 companies whose combined performance looks terrible over a particular period, presented in a way that encourages you to blame the result on the gender of the founders. And my point is not that women or men are better at running companies. My point is, how about we stop constantly trying to prove that women are worse or that men are worse. Men are still heavily overrepresented in top corporate positions. But there are also plenty of highly successful companies led by women. Some female-led companies outperform, some underperform. The same is true for companies led by men. It is almost as if what matters is the competence of the people involved, the quality of the business, the industry, the valuation, and the timing, not whether the person running it is a man or a woman.
